t:
(a) The Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (“BARDA”) may enter into a contract, for more 
than one but no more than 10 program years, for purchase of research services or of security countermeasures, as that term is defined in section 319F–2(c)(1)(B) of the PHS Act (42 U.S.C. 247d–6b(c)(1)(B)), if—
        (1) funds are available and obligated—
            (A) for the full period of the contract or for the first fiscal year in which the contract is in effect; and 
            (B) for the estimated costs associated with a necessary termination of the contract; and  
        (2) the Secretary determines that a multi-year contract will serve the best interests of the Federal Government by encouraging full and open competition or promoting economy in administration, performance, and operation of BARDA’s programs.  
    (b) A contract entered into under this section—
        (1) shall include a termination clause as described by subsection (c) of section 3903 of title 41, United States Code; and 
        (2) shall be subject to the congressional notice requirement stated in subsection (d) of such section.

fable.w: The section authorizes BARDA to enter multi-year procurement contracts when funds are available and the Secretary makes a best-interests determination. The tempting reading is that contracting with outside companies or the congressional notice requirement counts as participation, but contracts are not consultation on a federal decision, and notice to Congress stays inside the federal government. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: shall be subject to the congressional notice requirement stated in subsection (d) of such section.

opus.w: The section lets BARDA enter into multi-year contracts, which is contracting authority. The only process it requires is a notice to Congress, and Congress is inside the federal government. It might look like participation because companies are parties to the contracts and Congress gets formal notice, but contracting is excluded under the definition. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to comment on or challenge the decision.
opus.s: shall be subject to the congressional notice requirement stated in subsection (d) of such section.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to enter into contracts based on an internal determination of what serves the best interests of the Federal Government. While it mentions 'open competition,' this refers to the procurement process for vendors, which falls under the exclusion for 'applications for... contracts.' The definition explicitly states that applying for a contract is not participation. Furthermore, the only other interaction mentioned is a 'congressional notice requirement,' and Congress is inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary determines that a multi-year contract will serve the best interests of the Federal Government by encouraging full and open competition or promoting economy in administration, performance, and operation of BARDA’s programs.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "encouraging full and open competition" implies a public bidding process where outside companies participate. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" and states that applying for something is not participating in the decision. The section authorizes the *agency* to enter into contracts based on internal determinations of interest, not a process where outsiders consult on the decision to use multi-year contracts. The "congressional notice" is also internal (Congress is inside the government).
